## Load packages

`pacman` loads the required packages and installs any that are missing. `here::i_am()` places
this notebook in the repository, so paths resolve from the repository root. `fgsea` and
`enrichVolcano` (the user's own package, not on CRAN) are called with `::`.

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(
  here, dplyr, tibble, tidyr, purrr, stringr, limma, ggplot2, patchwork, readxl, writexl
)
here::i_am("03_Pathway_Enrichment/01_run_fgsea_and_fry/a_script/01_run_fgsea_and_fry.qmd")
```

## Read inputs

Every tested gene set is checked on every contrast with two methods. fgsea (fast gene set
enrichment analysis) ranks all proteins by a statistic and asks whether a set's members sit
towards the top or bottom of the ranking more than random sets of the same size. It is
competitive, comparing a set with the other proteins, and assumes proteins are exchangeable, which
they are not: proteins in a pathway move together. fry, from limma, is self-contained: it asks
whether the set's members move at all, using the sample-level data, so correlation between
members cannot inflate its null.

The inputs are the tested sets and their catalogue from `00_build_gene_sets`, the fitted
contrasts and design from stage 02, and the protein estimates from quantification, which fry reads
at the sample level.

```{r read}
stage <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry")
gene_sets <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data")
sets <- readRDS(file.path(gene_sets, "gene_sets.rds"))
gene_set_book <- file.path(gene_sets, "00_build_gene_sets.xlsx")
set_catalog <- read_excel(gene_set_book, "set_catalog")
protein_map <- read_excel(gene_set_book, "protein_gene_map")
fit <- readRDS(here("02_Differential_Expression", "02_Differential", "c_data", "fit.rds"))
d <- readRDS(here("02_Differential_Expression", "01_Design", "c_data", "design.rds"))
proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))
length(sets)
```

## Check alignment

A stale fit still lines up by count, so the checks compare names rather than lengths: proteins in
the fit, the protein map and the abundance matrix must match row for row, and the fit's
contrasts must match the design's.

```{r check}
contrast_names <- colnames(d$contrasts)
stopifnot(
  identical(rownames(fit$coefficients), protein_map$protein),
  identical(colnames(fit$coefficients), contrast_names),
  identical(rownames(proteins$E), protein_map$protein)
)
contrast_names
```

## Protein results

`topTable()` takes the fit and one contrast and returns one row per protein: log2 fold change,
average abundance, moderated t, p and BH-adjusted p. BH stays as `02_Differential` applied it,
within each contrast. The rows are stacked across contrasts and joined to the protein map.

`pi_score` is P.Value^|logFC| (Xiao et al. 2014, PMID 22321699), which combines effect size and
significance. It orders proteins within a contrast and selects nothing.

```{r protein-results}
protein_results <- map(set_names(contrast_names), function(contrast) {
  topTable(fit, coef = contrast, number = Inf, adjust.method = "BH", sort.by = "none") |>
    rownames_to_column("protein") |>
    select(protein, logFC, AveExpr, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val)
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "contrast") |>
  left_join(protein_map, by = "protein", relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  mutate(pi_score = P.Value^abs(logFC))
head(protein_results[c("contrast", "protein", "gene", "logFC", "t", "adj.P.Val", "pi_score")], 4)
```

Proteins up and down at FDR 0.05, per contrast.

```{r protein-summary}
protein_summary <- protein_results |>
  summarise(
    tested = n(),
    up = sum(adj.P.Val < 0.05 & logFC > 0),
    down = sum(adj.P.Val < 0.05 & logFC < 0),
    min_fdr = signif(min(adj.P.Val), 3), .by = contrast
  )
protein_summary
```

## Run fgsea

fgsea needs one ranked vector per contrast: the moderated t of each representative protein,
named by gene symbol so fgsea's leading edge comes back in the namespace the volcanoes label
with. The order of `ranked` matters, because the seeded fgsea calls draw their permutations in
this order.

```{r ranked}
ranked <- map(set_names(contrast_names), function(cn) {
  with(filter(protein_results, selected, contrast == cn), set_names(t, gene))
})
lengths(ranked)
```

For each set fgsea returns a p-value, its BH-adjusted `padj` over all sets in the contrast, the
NES (normalised enrichment score: positive when members sit towards the top of the ranking,
negative towards the bottom, scaled for set size) and the leading edge, the members that drive
the score.

```{r fgsea}
set.seed(1)
fgsea_raw <- map(ranked, function(stats) fgsea::fgsea(sets, stats, minSize = 15, maxSize = 500))
```

## Run fry

fry reads rows of `proteins$E`, so each set's gene symbols are turned into row numbers through
each symbol's representative protein. It reads limpa's precision weights through
`proteins$weights`. No `block`: participant is a fixed term in the design, and the residual
within-leg correlation is 0.027.

```{r fry-index}
selected_rows <- which(protein_map$selected)
set_rows <- map(sets, function(genes) {
  selected_rows[match(genes, protein_map$gene[selected_rows])]
})
proteins$weights <- fit$EList$weights
```

Both methods go into one long table, one row per set, contrast and method. Each package returns
its own BH column over the list it was given, fgsea's `padj` and fry's `FDR`; neither is
recomputed here. `NES` and `leadingEdge` exist for fgsea only.

```{r set-tests}
set_tests <- bind_rows(
  map(contrast_names, function(contrast) {
    as_tibble(fgsea_raw[[contrast]]) |>
      transmute(
        set_id = pathway, contrast, method = "fgsea", n = size,
        direction = if_else(NES > 0, "Up", "Down"), NES, p = pval, padj,
        leadingEdge
      )
  }),
  map(contrast_names, function(contrast) {
    fry(proteins, set_rows, d$design, d$contrasts[, contrast], sort = "none") |>
      rownames_to_column("set_id") |>
      transmute(
        set_id, contrast,
        method = "fry", n = NGenes,
        direction = Direction, NES = NA_real_, p = PValue, padj = FDR,
        leadingEdge = list(NULL)
      )
  })
)
table(set_tests$method)
```

## Collapse redundant sets

Collections overlap: glycolysis sits in all four. `fgsea::collapsePathways()` takes the
significant sets in order of p and keeps a set only if it is still significant given the leading
edge of a stronger set it overlaps; the kept sets are its `mainPathways`. It prunes without
re-adjusting, so the surviving FDR is conservative. Every set stays in the table; survivors are
marked `main = TRUE`.

```{r collapse}
main_sets <- map(set_names(contrast_names), function(contrast) {
  significant <- fgsea_raw[[contrast]][padj < 0.05][order(pval)]
  if (nrow(significant) < 2) {
    return(significant$pathway)
  }
  fgsea::collapsePathways(significant, sets, ranked[[contrast]], pval.threshold = 0.05)$mainPathways
})
lengths(main_sets)
```

Mark the survivors and add the catalogue columns.

```{r annotate-tests}
set_tests <- set_tests |>
  mutate(
    main = if_else(method == "fgsea", set_id %in% main_sets[[contrast[1]]], NA),
    .by = contrast
  ) |>
  left_join(
    select(set_catalog, set_id, database, pathway, source_size, description),
    by = "set_id"
  ) |>
  relocate(contrast, method, set_id, database, pathway)
head(select(set_tests, contrast, method, set_id, n, NES, p, padj, main), 4)
```

## Set summary

Significant sets per contrast at an adjusted p below 0.05, for fgsea, fgsea after collapse, and
fry. The baseline contrast sits in the table unflagged, for comparison.

```{r set-summary}
set_summary <- set_tests |>
  summarise(
    sets = n_distinct(set_id),
    fgsea = sum(method == "fgsea" & padj < 0.05),
    collapsed = sum(method == "fgsea" & padj < 0.05 & main),
    fry = sum(method == "fry" & padj < 0.05),
    .by = contrast
  )
set_summary
```

## Figures

The figures go to one A4 PDF, S1 to S7. `supplement()` takes a figure number, title and caption
text and returns a patchwork annotation with the supplement-style caption and panel tags.

```{r supplement-helper}
supplement <- function(number, title, text, tags = "A") {
  plot_annotation(
    caption = str_wrap(sprintf("S%d Figure. %s. %s", number, title, text), 115),
    tag_levels = tags,
    theme = theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9, lineheight = 1.2))
  )
}
```

The dot plots show four contrasts; the baseline contrast is left out. `survivors` holds the
significant fgsea sets that survived the collapse.

```{r survivors}
shown <- c("BFR_Post-Pre", "HLRT_Post-Pre", "Modality_x_Time_Interaction", "BFR_Post-HLRT_Post")
collections <- unique(set_catalog$database[set_catalog$qualifies])
survivors <- set_tests |>
  filter(method == "fgsea", padj < 0.05, main, contrast %in% shown) |>
  mutate(contrast = factor(contrast, shown))
count(survivors, contrast, .drop = FALSE)
```

`dotplot()` takes one contrast's survivors and draws the ten with the lowest adjusted p, NES on
the x axis and point size for set size. Colour is the collection when `by_database` is `TRUE`,
otherwise -log10 FDR. `sizes` and `fdr` fix the scales so panels on one page compare.

```{r dotplot-helper}
dotplot <- function(rows, by_database, sizes, fdr) {
  top <- rows |>
    slice_min(padj, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    mutate(label = enrichVolcano::clean_label(pathway, width = 45))
  colour <- if (by_database) {
    list(
      scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2", limits = collections, name = NULL),
      guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3)))
    )
  } else {
    scale_colour_viridis_c(
      option = "rocket", direction = -1, end = 0.9, limits = fdr,
      name = expression(-log[10] ~ FDR)
    )
  }
  ggplot(top, aes(NES, reorder(label, NES), size = n)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey75") +
    geom_point(
      aes(colour = if (by_database) database else -log10(padj)),
      alpha = 0.9, show.legend = TRUE
    ) +
    colour +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 5), limits = sizes, name = "genes") +
    labs(
      x = "normalised enrichment score", y = NULL,
      title = sprintf("%s, %d of %d survivors", rows$contrast[1], nrow(top), nrow(rows))
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), plot.title = element_text(size = 9))
}
```

`dotplot_figure()` stacks one dot plot per contrast that has a survivor, collects the legends and
adds the caption.

```{r dotplot-figure-helper}
dotplot_figure <- function(rows, number, name, by_database = FALSE) {
  by_contrast <- split(rows, rows$contrast, drop = TRUE)
  wrap_plots(
    map(by_contrast, dotplot,
      by_database = by_database, sizes = range(rows$n), fdr = range(-log10(rows$padj))
    ),
    ncol = 1, guides = "collect"
  ) +
    supplement(
      number, paste("Ten strongest collapse survivors,", name),
      paste0(
        paste(sprintf("(%s) %s.", LETTERS[seq_along(by_contrast)], names(by_contrast)),
          collapse = " "
        ),
        " Up to ten collapsePathways survivors per contrast, lowest adjusted p first; FDR is",
        " BH within contrast. Point size is the number of measured genes in the set; colour is ",
        if (by_database) "the collection" else "-log10 FDR",
        ". Contrasts with no survivor are omitted. Data: set_tests sheet of",
        " 01_run_fgsea_and_fry.xlsx."
      )
    )
}
```

S1 covers all collections, coloured by collection; S2 to S6 repeat it within each collection.

```{r dotplot-figures}
figures <- c(
  list(dotplot_figure(survivors, 1, "all collections", by_database = TRUE)),
  imap(collections, function(db, i) {
    dotplot_figure(filter(survivors, database == db), i + 1, db)
  })
)
```

S7 shows how much redundancy the collapse removed, rather than asserting it: significant sets
per collection and contrast, before and after.

```{r collapse-effect}
collapse_effect <- set_tests |>
  filter(method == "fgsea", padj < 0.05, contrast %in% shown) |>
  summarise(before = n(), after = sum(main), .by = c(contrast, database)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(before, after), names_to = "stage", values_to = "sets") |>
  mutate(stage = factor(stage, c("before", "after")), contrast = factor(contrast, shown))
figures <- c(figures, list(
  ggplot(collapse_effect, aes(stage, sets, fill = database)) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    facet_wrap(~contrast, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = NULL) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "significant sets") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    supplement(
      7, "Significant sets before and after collapse",
      paste(
        "Sets at FDR 0.05 per collection and contrast, before and after collapsePathways, which",
        "keeps a set only if it stands alone given a stronger set's leading edge. Data: set_tests",
        "sheet of 01_run_fgsea_and_fry.xlsx."
      ),
      tags = NULL
    )
))
```

Write all seven pages to `b_reports/01_run_fgsea_and_fry_figures.pdf`.

```{r write-figures}
pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry_figures.pdf"), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
walk(figures, print)
invisible(dev.off())
length(figures)
```

## Save results

`01_run_fgsea_and_fry.xlsx` holds `set_tests`, one row per set, contrast and method, with the
leading edge joined by `;`, and `protein_results`, every protein and contrast from the fit.
`02_`, `03_` and `08_` read both; `07_` reads `set_tests`.

```{r write}
sheets <- list(
  set_summary = set_summary,
  protein_summary = protein_summary,
  set_tests = mutate(set_tests, leadingEdge = map_chr(leadingEdge, paste, collapse = ";")),
  protein_results = protein_results
)
overview <- data.frame(
  sheet = names(sheets), rows = map_int(sheets, nrow), columns = map_int(sheets, ncol),
  description = c(
    "Significant sets per contrast and method",
    "Proteins up and down at FDR 0.05",
    "Every set test; main marks collapse survivors",
    "Every protein and contrast from the fit"
  )
)
write_xlsx(
  c(list(overview = overview), sheets),
  file.path(stage, "c_data", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry.xlsx")
)
```
